candidate.title: CPT-Seq
candidate.scope: The middle CPT-Seq row of the assigned Illumina poster crop: contiguity-preserving transposition sequencing with 96 indexed transposition reactions, pooling of DNA–transposase complexes, dilution into 96 new physical compartments, SDS release and compartment-indexed PCR. The two drawn lanes at each partitioning stage are representative wells among 96, not alternative methods or two samples. The graph records each drawn lane separately; the other 94 wells are implicit in the source caption. First-round lane A/B and second-round lane C/D are independent sets, joined by genuine pooling and repartitioning rather than one-to-one transfer. The crop also contains neighboring CAP-seq and RC-Seq workflows and cytosine structures; their labels and arrows do not make them targets of this CPT-Seq card. The verified secondary page heading and caption agree with this scope. Sequencing and haplotype reconstruction interpret the library but are not extra drawn operations.

method_scopes.rationale: CPT-Seq is the assigned card title and the middle-row label. The verified collection page is headed CPT-seq: Contiguity-Preserving Transposition Sequencing and captions the same ordered operations as A schematic overview of CPT-seq. The primary Amini paper explicitly describes the indexed-transposition/pooling/repartitioning/indexed-PCR architecture. CPT-seq capitalization variants and the expanded name denote the same scoped method. The two lanes depict parallel members of a 96-reaction population, with genuine mixing between the two partition stages. Neighboring CAP-seq/RC-Seq drawings, alternative partition counts, protease release, other sequencing platforms and scaffolding algorithms are outside this extraction.
